title: Refunded Qualifying Amount of a Returned Unit — Finch Circle Refund Accounting Rule
content:
**Rule.** When Finch Circle Loyalty Program points are taken back on a refunded return, the refunded qualifying amount is the qualifying amount on the unit's purchase points entries. When the refund deducted a restocking fee, the refunded qualifying amount is the refund amount less the sales tax refunded; when the refund was issued to a Merchandise Credit Card, it is the refund amount; otherwise it stays the qualifying amount on the unit's purchase points entries.

The refund amount, the sales tax refunded, any restocking fee deducted and the refund destination are read from the refund record of the return under Merchandise Purchases. The qualifying amount on the unit's purchase points entries is read from the membership's points history (its purchase points entry and any missing-points credit entry).

## Order of the tests

| Refund record shows | Refunded qualifying amount |
|---|---|
| a restocking fee deducted (greater than zero) | the refund amount less the sales tax refunded |
| no restocking fee, refund issued to a Merchandise Credit Card | the refund amount |
| neither | the qualifying amount on the unit's purchase points entries |

The restocking-fee test is read first: a refund with a restocking fee that was also issued to a Merchandise Credit Card takes the first row.

## Cases (hypothetical)

- A sofa with 900.00 on its purchase points entry is refunded 810.00 after a restocking fee, of which 60.00 is sales tax refunded: refunded qualifying amount 750.00.
- A sweater with 80.00 on its purchase points entry is refunded 86.40 to a Merchandise Credit Card, no restocking fee: 86.40.
- A lamp with 45.00 on its purchase points entry refunded to the original card, no restocking fee: 45.00.
